phase: R8 selection audit, no registered model study

entries.title: Sample, Mix, or Verify? Allocating Test-Time Compute under Imperfect Verifiers
entries.method: Pilot-calibrated distributions of difficulty, shared generator failures and verifier propensities feed an allocation planner; tests real verifier decisions and correlation/difficulty ablations.
entries.implication: Accuracy plus error correlation is established allocation prior work. Does not directly test a model reading synthetic error tables; that difference alone does not establish a new mechanism.
entries.access: primary full text read in stated sections

entries.title: Knowing Is Not Choosing: What Explicit Verification Adds Beyond Generative Preference
entries.method: Fresh candidate pools shared across likelihood and Yes/No verification selectors; confirmation cohorts, strict semantic criteria and blinded human audits separate recall/readouts from final choice.
entries.implication: Generic selecting versus generating and readable knowledge versus successful selection are already covered; not exact S2 verifier-choice duplication.
entries.access: primary methods read; results body only partly read

entries.title: Automatic Model Selection with Large Language Models for Reasoning
entries.method: LLM chooses between provided CoT and PAL reasoning solutions using few-shot selection examples; analyzes complementary errors and imperfect selector success.
entries.implication: Model selecting between methods itself predates S2. Choosing a future verifier from full error tables differs, but needs more than a new table/task to establish contribution.

entries.title: Overthinking the Truth: Understanding how Language Models Process False Demonstrations
read_sections: 5 false induction selection and causal head ablations
entries.method: Fourteen classification tasks, prefix-matching head selection on a separate toy task, late attention versus MLP ablations and random-head controls; also tests promotion of attended false labels.
entries.implication: H1 direct copying from misleading context has an existing causal mechanism account. Canceled history is not identical to false demonstrations; exact equality is not asserted. A new pathway mask on one margin trace alone lacks a new principle.
entries.access: HTML404; official arXiv PDF body read

entries.title: Algorithmic Taint Tracking: Attention-Based Provenance Enforcement for Secure Tool-Augmented LLMs
entries.venue: NeurIPS2026 AI4GOOD workshop poster, not verified as main-track paper
read_sections: official venue abstract only via browser
entries.method: Official abstract describes an externally propagated parallel sideband tensor using model attention, with modular logit gating.
entries.implication: This is not evidence that the base LLM learns explicit trace policy judgments. Claude claim that it exhausts the internal-vs-external distinction is too broad. No precise novelty ruling based only on this abstract.
entries.access: web parser unavailable; browser official poster page read. OpenReview text fetch presents verification challenge; full methods remain UNVERIFIED.

entries.title: Status of claimed exact NeuroTaint overlap
entries.implication: Multi-source/topical overlap controls were read, but equality of unused allowed values with a fixed forbidden trace is not verified as an identical contrast. Do not accept Claude assertion of factual identity from abstract/conclusion inspection.
entries.access: prior primary body record retained; no exact-duplication claim

entries.title: LLMCAPLENS value-sensitive factors
read_sections: III summary/TableIII constant-folding and index sensitivity
entries.implication: Value reasoning and structural/semantic taint factors already occur in the benchmark. This does not by itself prove exact S1 equality-contrast duplication.

entries.title: Models Take Notes at Prefill: KV Cache Can Be Editable and Composable
read_sections: Appendix D read/write heads, causal direction and scrubbing
entries.method: Separates fixed field from changed rule, transplants downstream states, compares same-conclusion/different-input resampling and note/rest interventions; read/write and attention/MLP circuit controls.
entries.implication: Stored conclusions, input/conclusion dissociation and downstream reuse already have direct causal tests. Does not establish that spontaneous duplicate-computation identity versus coincidence is an exactly duplicated contrast. Current G1 still needs a competing-mechanism discriminator.
entries.access: primary full text in stated sections

entries.title: Cell-Based Representation of Relational Binding in Language Models
entries.method: PLS decodes entity/relation indices from controlled discourse activations; one-shot relational queries and subspace interventions evaluate binding.
entries.implication: A fresh relational probe/patch application alone is not a new question. The statement that attributes are uniquely bound does not by itself prove a word-type collision contrast is unstudied. No search-absence firstness claim.

entries.title: Mixing Mechanisms v2 scope recheck
read_sections: keyword search scope only; prior v1 methods audit retained
entries.implication: No matched keyword for duplicate/unique/repeated is not evidence that collision tests are absent. Do not manufacture a novelty gap from this search.
entries.access: v2 full page available; exact collision coverage NOT_VERIFIED

rule: Separate methods actually read from abstracts; reject an investment for insufficient new contribution without asserting proven exact prior duplication.
